assessments.reasoning: Bytes [6869, 7048) of the pinned publisher text contain the complete section 4(d), including the acknowledging actor and the scope of the no-duty language. The reported range digest matches the binding. The opening distribution notice and the operative provisions are consistent with the distinction between publisher and external Affirmer.

challenge.method: Compared Creative Commons publishing the instrument with an external Affirmer applying it to a Work. Tested whether section 4(d) assigns Creative Commons a role under independent dealings.
challenge.results: Publication identifies the source of the instrument. The Statement of Purpose identifies the person associating CC0 with the Work as the Affirmer, and sections 2 and 3 attribute the waiver and fallback grant to that person. Publication alone supplies no evidence that Creative Commons applied CC0 to the Work. Section 4(d) neither creates nor resolves a duty under independent dealings.

limitations: The acknowledgment does not establish factual control of a particular Work or resolve duties arising from independent undertakings or jurisdiction-specific law.
reasoning: Section 4(d) records the Affirmer’s acknowledgment that Creative Commons is not a party to “this document” and has no duty or obligation “with respect to this CC0 or use of the Work.” Both phrases tie the acknowledgment to the instrument and the Work.
